subject.title: Reject split outbound agent session ownership

question: Should queued deliveries persisted by older releases with split ownership be migrated, surfaced for operator resolution, or intentionally dead-lettered when this invariant is introduced?
rationale: The current queue record does not prove which conflicting owner was intended, so code review cannot safely choose between preserving delivery, changing ownership, or permanently failing a user message.

options.title: Add an explicit upgrade path
options.body: Introduce a bounded migration or operator-visible repair flow for pre-existing conflicting queue entries, then let normal runtime recovery enforce the canonical owner rule.

options.title: Accept permanent rejection
options.body: Document that upgrade may permanently reject affected pending outbound messages and obtain explicit maintainer approval for that compatibility and message-loss tradeoff.

options.title: Narrow this PR
options.body: Apply validation only to new admission paths and track persisted-queue migration as a separate, maintainer-owned change.

recommendation.title: Add an explicit upgrade path
recommendation.body: Introduce a bounded migration or operator-visible repair flow for pre-existing conflicting queue entries, then let normal runtime recovery enforce the canonical owner rule.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied discussion specifically identifies this person for review of the outbound/Gateway boundary affected by the compatibility choice.
